requirements.boundary: Interface names and explicit addresses form a union; an explicit address bypasses except-interface. Loopback is added only for a nonempty interface list.
First wildcard matches only with a remaining name byte; null selectors never match. Static unknown-name check uses per-address matches.
IPv4 IFA_LABEL selects an address; packet arrival uses real name. UDP label exception admits only the selected destination; wildcard TCP has no label exception.
IPv6 link-local listener scope is the interface index, even for the same address on multiple links; global address scope is zero.
Static mode retains listeners when addresses disappear and does not bind later addresses once initial DAD has completed.
Dynamic mode opens new addresses and closes last-owner listeners; duplicate owners retain one socket. Recreated interface changes index and link-local scope.
Tentative IPv6 participates in matching but is never bound; static and dynamic retry after maturity, without exiting or logging EADDRNOTAVAIL.
Static pending-DAD and dynamic binding preserve CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE for low DNS/TFTP ports after UID change.

Explicit addresses absent from snapshots are attempted. Successfully created unowned listeners remain unowned even if the address later gains/loses an interface; failed unowned addresses first created on a real interface are retired with the last owner. INAME_USED forbids recreating the latter as a fallback.
Both bind modes conflict; unknown static names fail after listeners are attempted. Occupied UDP or TCP fails startup in either bound mode. Dynamic only suppresses EADDRNOTAVAIL.

C: a successful UDP, TCP or TFTP transport sets iface->done for all three; missing transports do not reappear after blocker release. If all fail, an interface event retries the group. Authorized Rust F23: runtime-shared-dns-both/all recover every missing transport after a 2.2s retry window, retain healthy socket inodes and exact replies, and retire added addresses. Other profiles retain the C contract.
Static IPv4 uses bound-address access; wildcard/dynamic inspect ingress with loopback/UDP-label exceptions. Bound TCP uses socket access in both bound modes.
UDP/TCP reply source equals selected destination in IPv4/IPv6 and scoped paths.

Bound TFTP is constrained by selected DNS addresses and DHCP exclusions; dedicated TFTP names override DHCP exclusion but not bound DNS selection. Wildcard dedicated TFTP bypasses normal DNS interface admission.
Dynamic TFTP listener add/remove uses address/scope semantics; static DAD TFTP is deferred then binds, ordinary static address additions do not add TFTP.
Relay request admission shares interface/listen-address union and no-DHCP exclusions; reply ingress can be outside selected downstream, dynamic recreate refreshes ifindex.
Every daemon, peer and namespace exits; all listeners and fixture links disappear. SIGTERM process group cleanup is recorded.

LOG_WARNING is severity4. With this -d driver C defaults to LOCAL0 (PRI132); ordinary foreground -k defaults to DAEMON (PRI28). The exact failed to create listening socket for ADDRESS: strerror warning occurs once per failed transport in attempt order. Dynamic EADDRNOTAVAIL and socket-stage EPROTONOSUPPORT/EAFNOSUPPORT/EINVAL are silent; bind EINVAL is not silently suppressed.
